questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code protects the shared seat count from concurrent reservations? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does inventory_reserve use atomic_fetch_add for the hold id even though the mutex is already held when the id is assigned?
choices: It is required because pthread mutexes do not provide memory ordering
It is redundant here: every access to the counter happens inside the critical section, so a plain increment would behave the same
Without it, two holds could receive the same id because the mutex does not cover that line
It makes the hold id visible to other threads before the hold slot is filled

questions.prompt: A caller reserves 2 seats and gets hold id 7, then calls inventory_release(inv, 7) twice. What do the calls return and what happens to availability?
choices: The first returns 2; the second blocks because the hold is gone
Both return 0 because release only works from the thread that reserved
Both return 2 and the seats are returned twice
The first returns 2 and restores the seats; the second returns 0 and changes nothing

questions.prompt: When all MAX_HOLDS slots are in use and seats remain, what does a further reservation do?
choices: It returns RESERVE_HOLD_TABLE_FULL after releasing the mutex, leaving the seat count unchanged
It waits on the mutex until another thread releases a hold
It returns RESERVE_SOLD_OUT because no slot is free
